procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism (if not already registered); registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added, and takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Prepare the certificate application: the application must include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately.
Log in to the ministry e-services portal and choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
Fill in the application form and upload the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee online: AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000).
Submit the application and receive approval, or a return with comments to correct; print the approved certificate.

Ensure the certificate is issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import. It must bear the authorised signature and official seal of the competent authority.

Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India. If transit through another country is necessary, the goods must remain under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, or storage. If the invoice is issued by a third party, indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed, and keep supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.

Inference: a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
